view_changes.assessment: Private network/host-loopback denial changes service reachability, addresses and abstract-socket behavior. Custody needs the descriptor boundary, not a blanket theorem that all network use is forbidden. Remove/rework unless a full accepted-input/host-context refinement establishes irrelevance; investigate the least changing enforcing mechanism.

Blocking all external-domain UNIX server connections and socket create/rename/link outside private binds is wider than excluding transfer of admitted references. Cover own why3server placement, configured socket paths and all helper connections; REFERS does not preserve socket renames everywhere. Rework or discharge full behavior, including controlled successful cases.

Preventing mounts that expose/move admitted objects serves custody, but denying every mount/topology operation is broader. Preserve all original successful computation behavior and nested-namespace cases or redesign the narrower enforcement boundary.

nosuid does not preserve set-ID/file-capability exec semantics merely because bits are retained in stat. The installed maps include host root identity, so credential containment needs a sound design. Establish no such original accepted tool/helper use and all descendant exec paths, or rework the maps/enforcement; do not count these failures as accepted refusals.

Host R/GATE changes non-idmapped IPC/device/proc ownership, outside signal/ptrace access, keyrings and per-UID resource charging. Same-host-uid root-owned user namespaces were rejected incorrectly, so substitution necessity is not established. Re-evaluate the narrower candidate and full kernel-resource outcomes.

Omitted existing mounts, revealed underlying directories and blocked future propagation change accepted filesystem/credential/config contents. No-list/no-stat requirements do not prove those objects irrelevant to all original workloads. Rework topology or prove complete accepted-domain independence without touching prohibited surfaces during this review.

Private tmp/TMPDIR affects preexisting files, cross-process coordination and the lifetime/content of temporary directories; image noexec adds an executable-temporary restriction. Full original helper/config/input/resource behavior must be preserved; lack of a known use is not closure.

A protected writer/source root can serve the location criterion; removal of original records/snapshot access and mount-root rename/remove behavior are additional observable changes. Preserve necessary original consumers and original target outcomes, not merely source bytes and path strings.

Read-only empty masks protect frame originals but change path existence/visibility/write outcomes. Establish the masks actually cover the adopted root and preserve accepted behavior; protection is not authority to create a new target-world assumption.

Moving from user to system manager changes ancestor cgroup limits, accounting, OOM policy and scheduling/IO defaults, not just two local memory properties. Match every relevant effective original control and lifecycle outcome; analyze same-manager enforcing alternatives. TOOL-CLOSURE cannot simply assume kernel-enforced defaults irrelevant.

The lead-created source mount point is not an existing required input of materialize/dispatch. Its missing-path refusal and changed label logic are new accepted-case changes. Rework the protocol to preserve original materialization/dispatch behavior; this reviewer supplies no ruling that creates a gate or adds a prerequisite.

A Landlock domain changes stacking, ptrace and path/topology behavior. Define the complete mediated surface and preserve all originally accepted observations, including consequences of its MAKE_SOCK/REFER rights gradient. A same-name domain is not invisible to code.
